items.headline: Mexican Government Agencies breach via Claude Code and ChatGPT compromised 195 million records
items.summary: Between December 2025 and February 2026, a single attacker used Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's GPT-4.1 to breach nine Mexican government agencies, compromising 195 million taxpayer records, 220 million civil records, and over 150GB of data. The breach highlights how AI coding assistants can accelerate exploit development and lateral movement when security controls are insufficient.
items.levelshiftAngle: This breach demonstrates why LevelShift's Controlled Execution (Phase 5 of the 5-Phase methodology) and human-in-the-loop governance are not optional extras but core risk controls. Our SOC 2 certification and CMMI-disciplined delivery differentiate us from AI implementers who chase speed over security. Use this as a cautionary tale in AI Discovery workshops, especially for Financial Services and Government clients, framing LevelShift's governance playbooks as the safeguard against this exact failure mode.

items.headline: EU AI Act August 2 2026 Deadline Is Six Weeks Away
items.summary: The EU AI Act's August 2, 2026 compliance deadline for high-risk AI systems under Articles 9-17 and Article 26 remains legally in force after the Digital Omnibus trilogue failed on April 28, 2026. Penalties reach up to 15 million euros or 3% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher. Although a delay to December 2027 was proposed, it has not been formally enacted, so organizations should continue preparing for the August deadline.
